recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future detailed behavior changes for cqf-expression in questionnaires should be handled in SDC or the Extension Pack unless a new core issue explicitly asks for additional Clinical Reasoning source text.
issue_request: FHIR-28205 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked for clarification of CQF-Questionnaire use of cqf-expression on Questionnaire.item and whether behaviors such as calculated values, editability, deletion, and answer options were defined by the profile or downstream use cases. The final resolution was to deprecate CQIF-Questionnaire in favor of SDC questionnaire profiles and update documentation to reference the SDC IG.
initial_application: No git commit directly mentions FHIR-28205. The same change family appears to have been applied by bc30255627a58b5e899f1afd7a087806ab48ac23, which cites J#30204 and J#21005, removes CQF Questionnaire profile/example/IG files, and replaces the old Documentation Template CQF-Questionnaire narrative with a Structured Data Capture IG reference.
additional_context: FHIR-21005 requested withdrawing CQIF Questionnaire in favor of SDC, and FHIR-30204 requested eliminating CQF Questionnaire and pointing CQF documentation to SDC. FHIR-I WGM 202101 minutes record that CQF would point to SDC for using CQL with Questionnaires. The current Extension Pack cqf-expression definition also points questionnaire readers to SDC guidance and examples. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-28205-specific community record that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source/clinicalreasoning-knowledge-artifact-representation.html Documentation Template section states that Questionnaire can use expression extensions for dynamic behavior and that SDC provides profiles and guidance. The page is in build scope through publish.ini and source/hierarchy.xml, and current source has no CQF-Questionnaire/CQIF-Questionnaire/cqf-questionnaire stale references.
